text.abl_sentence: no residual 6.011 (stuck at the unigram level, 6.006); no FFN 2.702 (+0.43, with 54% fewer parameters); no attention 3.695, next to the bigram floor 3.616 as it must be; no norm 2.546 (+0.27); no position 2.375 (+0.10); one head instead of eight 2.282 at seed 0 and 2.327 at seed 1 (+0.006 and +0.063 against the baseline at the same seed).
text.abl_reading:
What the numbers say

No residual: the model learns nothing past token frequencies. Held-out 6.011 at lr 3e-3 and 6.011 at lr 1e-3, against the unigram cross-entropy 6.006: both runs sit on the line of a model that ignores context, and the greedy continuation of every prompt is a row of full stops. Without the sum, every sublayer must rebuild the whole representation instead of adding a correction, and the gradient reaches the embedding only through twelve stacked sublayers. Dong et al. (2021, {{arXiv 2103.03404|https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03404}}) prove the related failure for attention: without "skip connections or multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), the output converges doubly exponentially to a rank-1 matrix". A lower learning rate does not rescue it here, so it is not an instability; it is the architecture. This is the largest effect on the page.

No attention: exactly the predicted floor. Blocks with only an FFN let each position see its own token and position and nothing else, so the best such model is a bigram model. It ends at 3.695, 0.08 above the bigram cross-entropy counted from all 122M training tokens (3.616); the network saw a tenth of them. Its greedy text shows it: one plausible phrase, then the same token repeated ("the park." and then only line breaks). A known answer the run lands on is a check on the whole pipeline. Everything the baseline gains below 3.62 comes from attention reading more than one token back.

No FFN: +0.43, but it is also a smaller model. Attention-only blocks have 2,688,768 parameters against 5,836,032; the run cannot separate "no MLP" from "54% fewer parameters" (a parameter-matched version with 18 attention-only layers was not run; it would cost about three times the attention compute per step). At 2.70 it is still far below the bigram floor, so attention alone does most of the context work; the FFN adds per-token computation on top.

No norm: trains, but worse and more sensitive. 2.546 at lr 3e-3 (+0.27); at lr 1e-3 it falls further behind (3.061 against 2.464 for the normalised baseline at the same rate, root Block lab): the unnormalised stream grows with depth and the update size that suits it is different. At 6 layers it does not diverge; the stability story at depth is {{Normalisation, residuals and stability|n:3fd5c17b0d0d8163b50dc5e9d9240e89}}.

No position: +0.10, much less than "word order is invisible" suggests. The causal mask leaks order: position t averages over exactly t + 1 tokens, so the model can count (Haviv et al. 2022, {{arXiv 2203.16634|https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.16634}}: "causal attention enables the model to infer the number of predecessors that each token can attend to"). It agrees with the {{Positional Encodings|n:3c65c17b0d0d81a5b7c9e578fcdfac00}} child's NoPE run of the root model (2.3666 on the same 20 windows; on 100 windows this run gives 2.3987 against its 2.389), which also shows what a learned table costs past 256 tokens.

One head: a small cost that depends on the seed. Eight heads of 32 against one head of 256, same parameters and FLOPs: +0.006 at seed 0, +0.063 at seed 1 (mean +0.035; the baseline's own spread is about 0.02). At this size and budget, eight heads buy a few hundredths of a nat; Michel et al. (2019, {{arXiv 1905.10650|https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10650}}) found that "a large percentage of attention heads can be removed at test time without significantly impacting performance". One head did run about a third faster on MPS (55,029 against 40,711 tokens/s, rough), plausibly because fewer, larger kernels suit this GPU (not profiled). What does not transfer: at 4,096 wide a single head would have hd = 4,096 and one attention pattern per layer for everything; real models keep hd at 64 to 256.

What transfers from these toy ablations: the order (residual and attention are essential, the FFN and norm matter, positions and head count matter least at this size) and the known answers (unigram for a broken network, bigram for no attention). What does not: the size of the gaps for a model a thousand times larger trained a thousand times longer.
